chapter: New York, Dallas and Kansas City
title: Meeting Charlie Parker at a barbecue-place jam session
summary: Moore met Parker at a Saturday-night jam after the Spook Breakfast and later saw him in Europe.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah. I always heard of Charlie Parker. Charlie Parker. Finally, I had my horn Saturday night around one or two o'clock in the morning and we'd be drinking and there was a barbecue place next door, great barbecue, and low and behold a jam session started, cats were blowing, blowing up a storm
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

and in comes Charlie Parker. We got introduced and I said 'I know your reputation for a solo. Fine, I need you, Charlie. Great. Let's blow.' So we blew, and the guys would come in and before you know it, you'd rest a while, then you'd go back to blowing, and you never leave that place, sometimes you don't leave that place until Sunday morning, daylight. Sometimes till drinking and just blow. Just blow. And that was [my] noon guys would go in there, Introduction to Charlie Parker, he's a great, great fellow.
He's quite a young man then.

I saw Charlie in later years when I was in Europe. I saw Charlie for the last time before I had to come back to New York he had passed away, but knowing Charlie Parker was an inspiration. At that time I couldn't tell that he was on his way to do better things, would be known to be famous, to make records. I couldn't see the handwriting on the wall. He is going to be famous and we were young then.
